name: Expedited and user-initiated long jobs
plain: Jobs that start soon or run long after a user action: Android expedited and UIDT, iOS 26 continued processing.
meaning: These are the sanctioned ways to finish work the person started (upload, export). They need a visible progress surface, so apps can no longer quietly continue large jobs.

android.prompt_ui: Notification with progress required for UIDT
android.persistence: Per job; stopped if the user stops it in the task manager
android.note: Expedited quota per 24 h: Active 30 min, Working 15, Frequent 10, Rare 10, Restricted 5; UIDT has no fixed quota but needs a network constraint and notification

ios.permission: BGTaskSchedulerPermittedIdentifiers with continued-processing prefix; GPU entitlement for GPU work
ios.persistence: Tasks showing little progress are terminated first; starts in the foreground
ios.note: Starts from a foreground user action; must report progress; separate GPU entitlement

limits.headline: Can run jobs soon or for a long time after you tap something, with daily limits
limits.user_action: You tap Export, Upload or Process and the app keeps working after you leave
can: Start an expedited job that runs soon on Android
Run a long task started by you (user initiated job) on Android 14 and newer
Continue processing after you leave on iOS 26
Show progress while the job runs
cannot: Run past the daily quota for expedited jobs on Android (30 minutes at best, 5 when restricted)
Start a long job on iPhone without a foreground tap
Skip showing progress on iPhone with iOS 26
Use the GPU in the background without the Apple GPU entitlement
limits.differs: Android has daily quotas for expedited work and long jobs need a network constraint. iPhone 26 continued processing starts only from a foreground action.

story.what_it_is: Allowed ways to finish long jobs you started, like uploads or exports, with a visible progress notice.

marketing.name: User initiated data transfers
marketing.pitch: Android lets apps run long transfers you start, with a notification you can see and stop.

marketing.name: Continued processing tasks
marketing.pitch: iOS 26 lets an app keep working on a job you start, with progress shown on screen.

story.for_you: You start a big upload, a video export or a backup and then leave the app. You see a progress notice and can stop it. You are never in the dark about a long job.
story.for_makers: Makers get a proper way to finish heavy work after you leave the app. In return they must show progress. This stops apps from quietly running large jobs in the background.

use_cases.example: A video editor finishes exporting your clip after you switch apps.
A cloud app uploads a big folder and shows a progress bar in the notifications.
A game finishes downloading a large patch while you check messages.
A social app uploads a long video post after you leave.
A fitness app syncs a long workout file after the run.
A hidden kit used to run big jobs quietly, which new rules forbid.

story.android_note: Android has expedited jobs for short urgent work and user initiated transfers for long ones.
story.ios_note: iOS 26 adds continued processing for jobs you start in the app.

technical_bounds: iOS tasks are terminated first if progress is low

history.change: BGContinuedProcessingTask lets foreground started work continue with progress UI
